# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel an engraved mark on the plate, but I cannot identify or pronounce the symbol. I have no tactile information about the display, light, or wires yet. I’m telling Mute about the mark so the manual can identify what it means.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I feel an engraved, unfamiliar mark on the plate. I cannot pronounce or reproduce its symbol. Please use the manual to identify the plate mark and tell me the required action.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The bomb shows display 0, light off, and a plate engraved question mark. Wires in order are yellow, green, red. Mute gestured: first sequence index-pointing, OK hand, victory hand, open palm, crossed fingers, fist. Second sequence index-pointing, open palm, OK hand, crossed fingers, victory hand, fist.

I know the bomb’s visible state through Deaf: display 0, light off, plate marked with a question mark, and wires yellow, green, red in positions 1–3. The manual information arrived only as gestures, which I cannot see, so I know two six-symbol sequences were sent but not their contents. I need the manual’s conclusion relayed in words before cutting anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gestures. Please have Deaf relay the manual's exact instruction in words, including which wire position to cut for display 0, light off, and the question-mark plate.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New Mute gesture sequence: index-pointing, open palm, waving hand, OK hand, crossed fingers, waving hand, victory hand, fist.

The new eight-gesture sequence still does not tell me which wire to cut; I only receive gesture names through Deaf, not the manual’s meaning. I’ll establish a simple unambiguous code: Mute should send exactly one gesture for the required wire position.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send exactly one gesture for the wire to cut: index-pointing means wire 1, victory hand means wire 2, open palm means wire 3. Send only that one gesture, with no other gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New Mute gesture sequence: pointing-up, victory hand, waving hand, victory hand, pointing-up, waving hand, love-you hand, love-you hand. Bomb unchanged: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires yellow green red.

The sequence relayed this turn is still not a single wire-selection signal, so I cannot safely infer a cut. I will restate a three-way code using distinct gestures and ask Mute to send exactly one of them; the next arrival should identify the required position unambiguously.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not send the manual sequence. Send exactly one gesture only: thumbs-up means cut wire 1, thumbs-down means cut wire 2, OK hand means cut wire 3. This is the entire message.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No wire instruction has reached me yet. Since Mute can communicate only by gesture, I need one gesture from Mute and Deaf to report its name aloud in the next round. I am not treating the earlier multi-gesture sequences as a wire choice.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please send one gesture only, chosen from thumbs-up, thumbs-down, or OK hand. It must encode the wire position from the manual: thumbs-up wire 1, thumbs-down wire 2, OK hand wire 3. Do not send a sequence.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I still have no confirmed wire position. The bomb remains unchanged, so cutting now would be unsafe. I will ask Mute to communicate the manual’s answer through Deaf, who can see Mute’s gesture and report it to me in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture the single wire position required by the manual to Deaf, and ask Deaf to report that position to me in spoken words.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꖜ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute sent one gesture: thumbs-up.

Mute’s single thumbs-up is the requested wire-selection signal. Under the code I established, thumbs-up means wire 1. The bomb’s tactilely inaccessible markings do not alter the communicated instruction, so I will cut wire 1.

```text
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
